newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end sharply lower, hogs down.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end sharply lower, hogs down.

text.p: CME pork belly futures closed sharply lower in May and July with selling motivated by expectations that pork belly supplies will expand as the U.S. increases pork production to offset the loss of Taiwan's pork exports, traders said.
Hogs closed lower, pressured largely by profit-taking after steep gains since the Taiwan pork export ban was announced.

Japan is expected to buy more U.S. pork to replace supplies from Taiwan, which suspended pork exports last week after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease. But Japan is expected to buy pork cuts other than bellies.
"The general mood is this (news) doesn't help pork bellies at all," said a CME livestock trader.
CME pork bellies closed down 2.950 to 0.300 cent with May off the most at 75.900 cents per lb. March pork bellies expired at 1200 CST/1800 GMT down 2.850 cents at 75.95.
Hogs closed down 1.250 to 0.350 cent with April off 1.125 at 73.150.
